value: selected temperatures (Tpref) of 29 individuals ranged from 6.4 to 18.7 C and fell with body mass (logarithmic fit, p < 0.001)
units: categorical (preferred temperature in a rising gradient, range of individual Tpref against body mass)

source.authors: Mathias Schakmann, Emil Aputsiaq Flindt Christensen, John Fleng Steffensen, Morten Bo Søndergaard Svendsen
source.title: The Influence of Body Size on Behavioral Thermal Preference in Atlantic Cod (Gadus morhua): Larger Fish Favor Colder Waters

method: behavioural: individual fish in a circular tank with a stepwise rising temperature gradient, position observed for 15 min at each step
conditions: Wild cod caught by trawling and beach-seining in the Oresund (Helsingor, Denmark) in February 2017, held three weeks at 10 C in 30 permille seawater, fed chopped herring three times a week and fasted 5 to 9 days before trials. 29 fish, 4 to 2625 g (Discussion gives 2635 g in one place). Each fish tested singly; water started at 4 to 6 C and rose in 2 C steps (3.4 C per hour) to 20 C, so the gradient ran one way only and no order or side counterbalancing is described. Same Results: F(1) = 119.527 for the size relation; the width of the preferred thermal range (mean 5.8 C, SD 1.3) was independent of body mass (F(1) = 1.337, p = 0.264). The paper gives no overall mean Tpref and no slope or r value.
quote: We experimentally determined the temperature preference (Tpref) of 29 Atlantic cod (Gadus morhua) … and found that Tpref ranged from 6.4 °C to 18.7 °C and correlated negatively with fish body mass in a logarithmical fashion (… p < 0.001).
note: Quote read in four abutting pieces; two cuts are marked (the 4 g to 2625 g clause; the figure reference and F statistic). Authors, volume, issue and title checked on Crossref single-DOI lookup (CC BY 4.0 vor); page footer prints CC BY with 3.0 in metadata. Family and order from main for the same species (sense_hearing rows). Not on main or any desk branch (grep of fishes8120596 and species+trait). Preferred temperature in a rising gradient; wild fish held and fasted, not naive.

value: trammel nets with blue, green or white LEDs caught 21 to 53% more fish per unit effort than unlit nets (p < 0.001); red LED nets caught 14% fewer (p = 0.001)

source.authors: Mengjie Yu, Changdong Liu, Liyou Zhang, Yanli Tang
source.title: Application of light-emitting diodes (LEDs) fishing lights to improve catch rates of small-scale trammel net fishery in the Yellow Sea, China

method: field experiment: commercial trammel nets with LED lights of four colours versus unlit control nets, catch per unit effort
conditions: Wild fish taken from commercial grounds off Rizhao, Weihai and Yantai (Yellow Sea) in autumn 2021, 33 valid hauls (11, 13 and 9 per region), soak about 12 h. Five treatments: control (CT, no light), blue (BT, 465 nm), green (GT, 516 nm), red (RT, 633 nm) and white (WT, 456 nm peak) LEDs; 15 net units per area, three per treatment, deployed 200 m apart; LED luminous intensity 4.8 cd each. Sites chosen from seafloor topography and fishermen's advice; randomisation of treatment positions is not described. Analysed by negative binomial GLMM with trip as random effect. CPUE is a catch outcome in fishing gear, so lure and capture effects are not separated from avoidance or sensory thresholds, and no non-detection (animals not responding) is measured. Treatment-by-region interaction not significant. Same paper: for marbled flounder and stone flounder blue and white LEDs gave no significant difference, and for swimming crab only red raised catch.
quote: The BT, GT, and WT harvested significantly higher CPUE (21%-53%) than CT (p<0.001), while RT caught 14% fewer individuals, and this difference was significant (p=0.001; Table S2).
note: Sentence read in two abutting pieces and its start and end confirmed on the page. Page prints no licence sentence; Crossref single-DOI lookup gives CC BY 4.0 (vor) and the same four authors, volume 9 and article 1036979 (no issue). Family and order from main for the same species (sense_hearing rows). Catch in lit nets is an attraction/avoidance outcome in gear, not a sensitivity measure (cf. audits 317, 344, 347, 349); no non-detection disclosure beyond the red result. Not on main or any desk branch (grep of fmars.2022.1036979 and species+trait).

source.authors: Fanny Hellhammer, Hella Heidtmann, Fritjof Freise, Stefanie C. Becker
source.title: Effects of Color and Light Intensity on the Foraging and Oviposition Behavior of Culex pipiens biotype molestus Mosquitoes

method: behavioural: two-choice feeding bioassay in cages, ink-coloured 8% fructose, colour of the abdomen scored
conditions: Laboratory strains of Culex pipiens biotype molestus derived from mosquitoes collected in northern Germany in 2012 and 2013; Bugdorm cages 30 cm, about 200 unfed mixed-sex mosquitoes up to three days old per assay, each bioassay six replicates with independent batches; colour positions rotated each replicate; light 16:8 cycle (maximum 1600 lx), constant 130 lx or 0 lx. Red vs blue n 6,555 mosquitoes; at 0 lx the red-blue preference was not found. Same paper: red vs green preferred at all levels above 0 lx and at 0 lx only in males; red vs black, red was not preferred and black was favoured (adjusted p < 0.0001); the four-choice assay was descriptive only, with no tests. Feeding on a coloured sugar solution under dye, so dye chemistry is a possible confound; dye vs plain controls were run in oviposition only.
quote: A significant preference for red over blue was found for both female and male mosquitoes at light intensities higher than 0 lx (adjusted p < 0.0001 in all cases).
note: Sentence read in two abutting pieces, end confirmed. Crossref single-DOI lookup: same four authors, volume 13, issue 11, CC BY 4.0 vor (page prints CC BY 3.0). Accepted name Culex pipiens (molestus listed as synonym in gbif-names.tsv); family and order from main for the same species. Colony-reared, not wild. Not on main or any desk branch (grep of insects13110993 and species+trait).

value: healthy females spent significantly more time with the urine odour of a parasitised male than of a healthy male in a Y-maze (t = 2.94, df = 28, p = 0.032)
units: categorical (time with male urine odour, paired choice, t test)

source.authors: Heike Lutermann, Kemba B. Butler, Nigel C. Bennett
source.title: Parasite-Mediated Mate Preferences in a Cooperatively Breeding Rodent

method: behavioural: Y-maze two-choice test, 1 ml male urine on 20 g sawdust in each choice chamber, 20 min observation
conditions: Highveld mole-rats caught wild in suburban Pretoria (October 2008 to September 2009) and kept in colonies at 25 C, 12L:12D; the abstract names C. h. hottentotus, the introduction and results C. h. pretoriae. 30 non-breeding females (15 healthy, 15 infested with a cestode, Mathevotaenia sp., status from faecal proglottids; healthy animals dosed with ivermectin, infested with saline) and 30 males (15 and 15) as urine donors. Each female tested once with unfamiliar males, 6 h isolation beforehand; male urine reused once for healthy and once for infested females; infested-odour side alternated. Same Results: infested females showed no difference between the two odours (t = 0.30, p = 0.990), although the abstract says the opposite held for them, so the abstract overstates; no sawdust-only blank control described; healthy females entered chambers more often than infested ones; no main effect of female (p = 1.00) or male infestation (p = 0.396), only the interaction (F = 15.19, p = 0.0006). Odour contrast is infested versus healthy male urine, which also differs in the donor, so the value is a discrimination of urine odours, not a threshold.
quote: Healthy females spend significantly more time with the odor of the parasitized male than that of the healthy male (t = 2.94, df = 28, p = 0.032, Figure 2).
note: Sentence read whole in two abutting pieces. Crossref single-DOI lookup (CC BY 4.0 vor): same three authors, volume 10, article 838076, no issue; page prints no licence sentence. Family and order from main (Cryptomys hottentotus, Bathyergidae, Rodentia). Not on main or any desk branch (grep of 838076, Mathevotaenia and species trait).

value: UV-A LED lights fitted to lure-baited traps raised total moth catches 7-fold in July and 3-fold in August
units: categorical (fold change in trap catch against unlit baited traps, linear or generalised linear models with Tukey's HSD)

source.title: Optimizing UV-A Solar-Powered Lights to Enhance Lures for Codling Moth, Cydia pomonella L. (Lepidoptera: Tortricidae)

method: field experiment: solar-powered LED units on orange delta traps with a moth lure, against unlit traps with the same lure
conditions: Wild populations in commercial apple and pear orchards near Tieton and Wapato, Washington, in 2024 and 2025; ten trials (some organic, some conventional), 5 to 13 replicates in trials 1 to 8 and 27 to 53 in trials 9 and 10, trials of 6 to 34 days. Two lures: CM4K (dual-sex non-pheromone) and PH1X (1 mg codlemone), so total catch pools both sexes and the light effect is on top of an olfactory lure that was present in every trap; the moth is drawn to the trap, no threshold or non-detection of light is measured. One trap of each type per orchard row, 30 m apart at about 3 m, placement randomised; peak wavelengths 365 to 397 nm for six UV units (best 395 nm, 1000 to 2000 mW/m2 per the abstract), plus blue-green-red and green units; zero-catch treatments excluded from analysis. Same abstract: adding UV-A lights did not increase moth catches early in the season with either lure; in mid-season trials only some UV units beat unlit traps, and the green and BGR lights did not differ from unlit traps. Non-target insects also increased with lights. Irradiance fell more than 90% at 15 cm.
quote: However, UV-A LEDs, when used with these two lures, significantly increased total moth catches 7- and 3-fold in July and August, respectively.
note: Sentence read whole in two abutting pieces. Crossref single-DOI lookup: same two authors, volume 17, issue 4, CC BY 4.0 vor (page metadata CC BY 3.0, no sentence). Family and order from main for the same species (acuity rows). Not on main or any desk branch (grep of insects17040354 and species+behaviour_vision). Lure/trap catch outcome in orchards, so a field attraction result and not a sensory threshold.
